# Commands

12 commands in three categories. Each has a playbook the model loads on demand; the playbooks are the actual behaviour, and they live in [`skill/reference/`](../skill/reference/).

## Establish

### `/airtight init`

Capture durable security truth in THREATS.md and CONTROLS.md

*When to use:* Inspects the repository, interviews on material gaps only, and writes THREATS.md and CONTROLS.md plus the machine-readable control register. Use when the user wants to get started with security, or when another command reports missing security context.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/init.md)

### `/airtight threat-model [feature]`

STRIDE per trust boundary, before the code exists

*When to use:* STRIDE per trust boundary plus abuse cases, producing the controls the design needs. Use when the user is designing something and asks what could go wrong.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/threat-model.md)

## Evaluate

### `/airtight review [target]`

Deep reasoning review: reachability, authorization, control drift

*When to use:* Dual-subagent with adversarial verification. Use when the user asks whether something is exploitable, or wants a real review rather than a scan.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/review.md)

### `/airtight audit [target]`

Deterministic sweep across enabled domains, scored per domain

*When to use:* Documents, does not fix. Use when the user wants the overall security posture or asks for a security check of the whole repository.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/audit.md)

### `/airtight triage [report]`

Ingest, deduplicate, and triage SARIF/Snyk/Trivy reports

*When to use:* Use when the user provides a vulnerability scan export, mentions SARIF or Dependabot alerts, or asks to triage external security scanner results.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/triage.md)

### `/airtight attest [framework]`

Export machine-verified control evidence for SOC 2 / ISO 27001

*When to use:* Verifies automated controls, checks SLA overdue status, and generates proof packages. Use when preparing for a security audit, verifying SOC 2 or ISO compliance, or exporting control evidence.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/attest.md)

### `/airtight secrets`

Credential scan of the working tree and git history

*When to use:* Use when the user mentions leaked keys, committed secrets, or asks whether anything sensitive is in the repository.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/secrets.md)

### `/airtight deps`

Dependency and advisory review with honest reachability

*When to use:* Use when the user asks about vulnerable dependencies, CVEs, or supply-chain risk in packages.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/deps.md)

### `/airtight supply-chain`

CI/CD hardening, provenance, and build integrity

*When to use:* CI triggers, token scope, action pinning, runners, provenance. Use when the user asks about CI security, GitHub Actions hardening, or build integrity.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/supply-chain.md)

### `/airtight infra`

IaC posture: Terraform, Kubernetes, containers

*When to use:* Use when the user asks about cloud posture, IaC security, or container hardening.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/infra.md)

### `/airtight correlate [paths]`

Correlate IaC exposure with application routes and sinks

*When to use:* Use when the user wants to understand external attack surface exposure, bridge IaC ingress with application code, or verify whether code vulnerabilities are reachable from the internet.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/correlate.md)

## Fix

### `/airtight harden [target]`

Apply remediations in triage order and verify once

*When to use:* The only command that edits. Use when the user asks to fix findings or to make something secure.

[Playbook](../skill/reference/harden.md)

## Infrastructure verbs

Not commands the model routes to, but things you run:

```bash
airtight hooks on | off | status
airtight hooks ignore-value <rule> "<value>" --reason "..."
airtight detect [paths] [--json] [--tier immediate] [--pack <name>] [--baseline <path>] [--since <ref>]
airtight findings sync | list | accept | overdue
airtight controls verify | coverage --framework <name>
airtight context
```

Exit codes are the contract: `0` clean, `1` the engine failed, `2` findings present or a control failing.
